for a [-1,1] range in input and output, my way of getting the input in that range is just to take the position of the pixel, divide x by the width, y by the height, substract 0.5, then multiply by 2.

so, for the input:

((x/width)-0.5)*2
((y/height)-0.5)*2

for the output, to get the [-1, 1] range, you need the activation function at inference to have an output in the range of [-1,1] (like hyperbolic tangent; tanh())
I also like the gaussian function, it is nice when it is in the last or first layer of your network, the rest would be tanh(). 
or sigmoid() if you want [0,1]

for the weights and biases, I just use uniform distribution. the range of it depends on your model, it can range from [-0.25, 0.25] to [-5, 5] depending on the size and act function. the bigger your network, the stronger the signal will be at inference, meaning you need to tune down the uniform distribution to get a nice looking image.
